root_cause.mechanism: When running a Python script directly (e.g. as __main__), importlib.util.find_spec("__main__") raises ValueError: __main__.__spec__ is None if __spec__ is None. Flask's get_root_path and _find_package_path called importlib.util.find_spec without handling ValueError, causing application instantiation to fail.

hypotheses.text: importlib.util.find_spec("__main__") raises ValueError when __main__.__spec__ is None, which occurs when running a script directly without a spec (or similar circumstances). _find_package_path calls importlib.util.find_spec(root_mod_name) without catching ValueError for root_mod_name == '__main__' (or catches it only under certain conditions or not when root_spec is looked up).
hypotheses.predicts: Passing '__main__' to importlib.util.find_spec raises ValueError: __main__.__spec__ is None when __spec__ is None on sys.modules['__main__'], and handling ValueError around importlib.util.find_spec in _find_package_path (and anywhere else) will gracefully fall back to current working directory or sys.modules['__main__'].
hypotheses.evidence: importlib.util.find_spec("__main__") raises ValueError: __main__.__spec__ is None when running Flask("__main__") with __spec__ = None, affecting both get_root_path and _find_package_path.

hypotheses.text: Checking if import_name or root_mod_name is '__main__' or catching ValueError specifically around importlib.util.find_spec will avoid calling find_spec on __main__.
hypotheses.predicts: Checking root_mod_name == '__main__' before calling importlib.util.find_spec (or checking sys.modules.get(import_name)) will prevent importlib.util.find_spec from raising ValueError for '__main__'.
hypotheses.evidence: Both get_root_path and _find_package_path call importlib.util.find_spec on import_name / root_mod_name without handling the ValueError raised when import_name == '__main__' or when __main__.__spec__ is None.
